summary: Suffolk County, NY platform tower of about 70 ft; a 1922 plan and a 1933 petition to move it are reported, and it is now listed as gone with no removal date found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no removal date, fate or site description in the sources read

events.note: Brooklyn Daily Eagle (April 6, 1922) reported that W.G. Howard, Assistant Superintendent of State forests, backed Fire Warden Wohlfarth's plan to move the tower from South Side Club property to his land in Central Islip; completion not stated
Warden Robert Wohlfarth petitioned the Islip Town Board (April 27, 1933) to move the 70-foot tower from his late father's yard to his own back yard

notes_for_editor: The only history found is two 1920s-1930s newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; we did not open the originals. The 1922 plan and the 1933 petition may concern the same tower and the same family (Fire Warden Wohlfarth and his son), but no source says so, so the story does not link them. Searches found no account of the tower's end or of the site today. Two searches returned the Central Islip former firehouse and the South Side Sportsmen's Club, which are not lookouts and are not used. The brief's 21.3 m matches the 70-foot height in the 1933 notice; no correction proposed. Two WebSearch calls were used for this lookout.
